comment: Allowlist seccomp profile for the ts-sandbox-harness container. Default action is ERRNO: any syscall not listed fails with EPERM.

Exercised in CI on GitHub's Ubuntu runners under both runc and runsc (see .github/workflows/sandbox.yml). Re-run scripts/check-sandbox.sh on any new host; if node fails to start, scripts/diagnose-seccomp.sh shows which rule is responsible.

Under gVisor this profile is only enforced if runsc is registered with --oci-seccomp (see README). Without that flag gVisor ignores it; gVisor's own syscall interception still protects the host kernel.

Deliberately absent vs Docker's default profile: all socket syscalls (the container has no network and Node needs none here), io_uring_*, memfd_create, ptrace, process_vm_*, bpf, perf_event_open, userfaultfd, unshare/setns/mount, keyring, kexec, module loading, personality, fork/vfork.

clone is allowed ONLY for threads: (flags & (CLONE_THREAD | namespace flags)) must equal CLONE_THREAD. Node creates threads and never needs a process, so glibc fork()/libuv -- and therefore child_process, even after an escape from the vm context -- cannot create one. See the clone3 note below for the path this does not cover.

clone3 is ALLOWED, unfiltered. Verified in CI (scripts/diagnose-seccomp.sh): under gVisor with --oci-seccomp, any profile that refuses clone3 -- Docker's own default included -- makes glibc's pthread_create fail, because the refusal does not surface as the ENOSYS that triggers glibc's fallback to clone. clone3 passes its flags in a struct, which seccomp cannot inspect, so it cannot be restricted to threads. Consequence: the thread-only guarantee covers every process-creation path that goes through glibc fork() or libuv (which use clone), i.e. everything reachable from JavaScript including child_process; a raw clone3 syscall from native code is not covered. Reaching that requires a V8 exploit inside gVisor, and --pids-limit remains the backstop.

syscalls.comment: File and descriptor I/O. Read-only rootfs and a noexec tmpfs bound what these can reach.
Memory management, including protection keys V8 may use for W^X code pages.
Event loop (libuv): epoll, eventfd, timers, signals.
Threads, scheduling, time, identity and process housekeeping.

Threads only: (flags & (CLONE_THREAD|CLONE_NEWNS|CLONE_NEWCGROUP|CLONE_NEWUTS|CLONE_NEWIPC|CLONE_NEWUSER|CLONE_NEWPID|CLONE_NEWNET)) == CLONE_THREAD. 0x7E030000 = 2114125824, CLONE_THREAD = 0x10000 = 65536. Argument 0 is flags on x86_64 and aarch64.
Must be allowed for node to start under gVisor; see top-level comment for the security trade-off.
